kjv: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.

vulg: quod cum audisset filius sororis Pauli insidias venit et intravit in castra nuntiavitque Paulo
clem: Quod cum audisset filius sororis Pauli insidias, venit, et intravit in castra, nuntiavitque Paulo.
tr: ακουσας δε ο υιος της αδελφης παυλου το ενεδρον  την ενεδραν  παραγενομενος και εισελθων εις την παρεμβολην απηγγειλεν τω παυλω
kjv: And when Paul's sister's son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.

vulg: vocans autem Paulus ad se unum ex centurionibus ait adulescentem hunc perduc ad tribunum habet enim aliquid indicare illi
clem: Vocans autem Paulus ad se unum ex centurionibus, ait: Adolescentem hunc perduc ad tribunum, habet enim aliquid indicare illi.
tr: προσκαλεσαμενος δε ο παυλος ενα των εκατονταρχων εφη τον νεανιαν τουτον απαγαγε προς τον χιλιαρχον εχει γαρ τι απαγγειλαι αυτω
kjv: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.

vulg: et ille quidem adsumens eum duxit ad tribunum et ait vinctus Paulus vocans rogavit me hunc adulescentem perducere ad te habentem aliquid loqui tibi
clem: Et ille quidem assumens eum duxit ad tribunum, et ait: Vinctus Paulus rogavit me hunc adolescentem perducere ad te, habentem aliquid loqui tibi.
tr: ο μεν ουν παραλαβων αυτον ηγαγεν προς τον χιλιαρχον και φησιν ο δεσμιος παυλος προσκαλεσαμενος με ηρωτησεν τουτον τον νεανιαν αγαγειν προς σε εχοντα τι λαλησαι σοι
kjv: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.

vulg: adprehendens autem tribunus manum illius secessit cum eo seorsum et interrogavit illum quid est quod habes indicare mihi
clem: Apprehendens autem tribunus manum illius, secessit cum eo seorsum, et interrogavit illum: Quid est quod habes indicare mihi?
tr: επιλαβομενος δε της χειρος αυτου ο χιλιαρχος και αναχωρησας κατ ιδιαν επυνθανετο τι εστιν ο εχεις απαγγειλαι μοι
kjv: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that thou hast to tell me?

vulg: ille autem dixit Iudaeis convenit rogare te ut crastina die Paulum producas in concilium quasi aliquid certius inquisituri sint de illo
clem: Ille autem dixit: Judis convenit rogare te ut crastina die producas Paulum in concilium, quasi aliquid certius inquisituri sint de illo:
tr: ειπεν δε οτι οι ιουδαιοι συνεθεντο του ερωτησαι σε οπως αυριον εις το συνεδριον καταγαγης τον παυλον ως μελλοντες τι ακριβεστερον πυνθανεσθαι περι αυτου
kjv: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.

vulg: tu vero ne credideris illis insidiantur enim ei ex eis viri amplius quadraginta qui se devoverunt non manducare neque bibere donec interficiant eum et nunc parati sunt expectantes promissum tuum
clem: tu vero ne credideris illis: insidiantur enim ei ex eis viri amplius quam quadraginta, qui se devoverunt non manducare, neque bibere donec interficiant eum: et nunc parati sunt, exspectantes promissum tuum.
tr: συ ουν μη πεισθης αυτοις ενεδρευουσιν γαρ αυτον εξ αυτων ανδρες πλειους τεσσαρακοντα οιτινες ανεθεματισαν εαυτους μητε φαγειν μητε πιειν εως ου ανελωσιν αυτον και νυν ετοιμοι εισιν προσδεχομενοι την απο σου επαγγελιαν
kjv: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.

vulg: tribunus igitur dimisit adulescentem praecipiens ne cui loqueretur quoniam haec nota sibi fecisset
clem: Tribunus igitur dimisit adolescentem, prcipiens ne cui loqueretur quoniam hc nota sibi fecisset.
tr: ο μεν ουν χιλιαρχος απελυσεν τον νεανιαν παραγγειλας μηδενι εκλαλησαι οτι ταυτα ενεφανισας προς με
kjv: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.

vulg: et vocatis duobus centurionibus dixit illis parate milites ducentos ut eant usque Caesaream et equites septuaginta et lancearios ducentos a tertia hora noctis
clem: Et vocatis duobus centurionibus, dixit illis: Parate milites ducentos ut eant usque Csaream, et equites septuaginta, et lancearios ducentos a tertia hora noctis,
tr: και προσκαλεσαμενος δυο τινας των εκατονταρχων ειπεν ετοιμασατε στρατιωτας διακοσιους οπως πορευθωσιν εως καισαρειας και ιππεις εβδομηκοντα και δεξιολαβους διακοσιους απο τριτης ωρας της νυκτος
kjv: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;

vulg: et iumenta praeparate ut inponentes Paulum salvum perducerent ad Felicem praesidem
clem: et jumenta prparate ut imponentes Paulum, salvum perducerent ad Felicem prsidem.
tr: κτηνη τε παραστησαι ινα επιβιβασαντες τον παυλον διασωσωσιν προς φηλικα τον ηγεμονα
kjv: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.

clem: (Timuit enim ne forte raperent eum Judi, et occiderent, et ipse postea calumniam sustineret, tamquam accepturus pecuniam.)
tr: γραψας επιστολην περιεχουσαν τον τυπον τουτον
kjv: And he wrote a letter after this manner:

vulg: scribens epistulam continentem haec Claudius Lysias optimo praesidi Felici salutem
clem: Scribens epistolam continentem hc: Claudius Lysias optimo prsidi Felici, salutem.
tr: κλαυδιος λυσιας τω κρατιστω ηγεμονι φηλικι χαιρειν
kjv: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.

vulg: virum hunc conprehensum a Iudaeis et incipientem interfici ab eis superveniens cum exercitu eripui cognito quia Romanus est
clem: Virum hunc comprehensum a Judis, et incipientem interfici ab eis, superveniens cum exercitu eripui, cognito quia Romanus est.
tr: τον ανδρα τουτον συλληφθεντα υπο των ιουδαιων και μελλοντα αναιρεισθαι υπ αυτων επιστας συν τω στρατευματι εξειλομην αυτον μαθων οτι ρωμαιος εστιν
kjv: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.

vulg: volensque scire causam quam obiciebant illi deduxi eum in concilium eorum
clem: Volensque scire causam quam objiciebant illi, deduxi eum in concilium eorum.
tr: βουλομενος δε γνωναι την αιτιαν δι ην ενεκαλουν αυτω κατηγαγον αυτον εις το συνεδριον αυτων
kjv: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:

vulg: quem inveni accusari de quaestionibus legis ipsorum nihil vero dignum morte aut vinculis habentem crimen
clem: Quem inveni accusari de qustionibus legis ipsorum, nihil vero dignum morte aut vinculis habentem criminis.
tr: ον ευρον εγκαλουμενον περι ζητηματων του νομου αυτων μηδεν δε αξιον θανατου η δεσμων εγκλημα εχοντα
kjv: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.

vulg: et cum mihi perlatum esset de insidiis quas paraverunt ei misi ad te denuntians et accusatoribus ut dicant apud te
clem: Et cum mihi perlatum esset de insidiis quas paraverant illi, misi eum ad te, denuntians et accusatoribus ut dicant apud te. Vale.
tr: μηνυθεισης δε μοι επιβουλης εις τον ανδρα μελλειν εσεσθαι υπο των ιουδαιων εξαυτης επεμψα προς σε παραγγειλας και τοις κατηγοροις λεγειν τα προς αυτον επι σου ερρωσο
kjv: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.

vulg: milites ergo secundum praeceptum sibi adsumentes Paulum duxerunt per noctem in Antipatridem
clem: Milites ergo secundum prceptum sibi assumentes Paulum, duxerunt per noctem in Antipatridem.
tr: οι μεν ουν στρατιωται κατα το διατεταγμενον αυτοις αναλαβοντες τον παυλον ηγαγον δια της νυκτος εις την αντιπατριδα
kjv: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.

vulg: et postera die dimissis equitibus ut irent cum eo reversi sunt ad castra
clem: Et postera die dimissis equitibus ut cum eo irent, reversi sunt ad castra.
tr: τη δε επαυριον εασαντες τους ιππεις πορευεσθαι συν αυτω υπεστρεψαν εις την παρεμβολην
kjv: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:

vulg: qui cum venissent Caesaream et tradidissent epistulam praesidi statuerunt ante illum et Paulum
clem: Qui cum venissent Csaream, et tradidissent epistolam prsidi, statuerunt ante illum et Paulum.
tr: οιτινες εισελθοντες εις την καισαρειαν και αναδοντες την επιστολην τω ηγεμονι παρεστησαν και τον παυλον αυτω
kjv: Who, when they came to Caesarea and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.

vulg: cum legisset autem et interrogasset de qua provincia esset et cognoscens quia de Cilicia
clem: Cum legisset autem, et interrogasset de qua provincia esset, et cognoscens quia de Cilicia:
tr: αναγνους δε ο ηγεμων και επερωτησας εκ ποιας επαρχιας εστιν και πυθομενος οτι απο κιλικιας
kjv: And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;

vulg: audiam te inquit cum et accusatores tui venerint iussitque in praetorio Herodis custodiri eum
clem: Audiam te, inquit, cum accusatores tui venerint. Jussitque in prtorio Herodis custodiri eum.
tr: διακουσομαι σου εφη οταν και οι κατηγοροι σου παραγενωνται εκελευσεν τε αυτον εν τω πραιτωριω του ηρωδου φυλασσεσθαι
kjv: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's judgment hall.

vulg: post quinque autem dies descendit princeps sacerdotum Ananias cum senioribus quibusdam et Tertullo quodam oratore qui adierunt praesidem adversus Paulum
clem: Post quinque autem dies descendit princeps sacerdotum Ananias, cum senioribus quibusdam, et Tertullo quodam oratore, qui adierunt prsidem adversus Paulum.
tr: μετα δε πεντε ημερας κατεβη ο αρχιερευς ανανιας μετα των πρεσβυτερων και ρητορος τερτυλλου τινος οιτινες ενεφανισαν τω ηγεμονι κατα του παυλου
kjv: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.

vulg: et citato Paulo coepit accusare Tertullus dicens cum in multa pace agamus per te et multa corrigantur per tuam providentiam
clem: Et citato Paulo cpit accusare Tertullus, dicens: Cum in multa pace agamus per te, et multa corrigantur per tuam providentiam,
tr: κληθεντος δε αυτου ηρξατο κατηγορειν ο τερτυλλος λεγων (24:3) πολλης ειρηνης τυγχανοντες δια σου και κατορθωματων γινομενων τω εθνει τουτω δια της σης προνοιας
kjv: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,

vulg: semper et ubique suscipimus optime Felix cum omni gratiarum actione
clem: semper et ubique suscipimus, optime Felix, cum omni gratiarum actione.
tr: παντη τε και πανταχου αποδεχομεθα κρατιστε φηλιξ μετα πασης ευχαριστιας
kjv: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.

vulg: ne diutius autem te protraham oro breviter audias nos pro tua clementia
clem: Ne diutius autem te protraham, oro, breviter audias nos pro tua clementia.
tr: ινα δε μη επι πλειον σε εγκοπτω παρακαλω ακουσαι σε ημων συντομως τη ση επιεικεια
kjv: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.

vulg: invenimus hunc hominem pestiferum et concitantem seditiones omnibus Iudaeis in universo orbe et auctorem seditionis sectae Nazarenorum
clem: Invenimus hunc hominem pestiferum, et concitantem seditiones omnibus Judis in universo orbe, et auctorem seditionis sect Nazarenorum:
tr: ευροντες γαρ τον ανδρα τουτον λοιμον και κινουντα στασιν πασιν τοις ιουδαιοις τοις κατα την οικουμενην πρωτοστατην τε της των ναζωραιων αιρεσεως
kjv: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:

vulg: qui etiam templum violare conatus est quem et adprehendimus
clem: qui etiam templum violare conatus est, quem et apprehensum voluimus secundum legem nostram judicare.
tr: ος και το ιερον επειρασεν βεβηλωσαι ον και εκρατησαμεν και κατα τον ημετερον νομον ηθελησαμεν κρινειν
kjv: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.

clem: Superveniens autem tribunus Lysias, cum vi magna eripuit eum de manibus nostris,
tr: παρελθων δε λυσιας ο χιλιαρχος μετα πολλης βιας εκ των χειρων ημων απηγαγεν
kjv: But the chief captain Lysias came upon us, and with great violence took him away out of our hands,

vulg: a quo poteris ipse iudicans de omnibus istis cognoscere de quibus nos accusamus eum
clem: jubens accusatores ejus ad te venire: a quo poteris ipse judicans, de omnibus istis cognoscere, de quibus nos accusamus eum.
tr: κελευσας τους κατηγορους αυτου ερχεσθαι επι σε παρ ου δυνηση αυτος ανακρινας περι παντων τουτων επιγνωναι ων ημεις κατηγορουμεν αυτου
kjv: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.

vulg: adiecerunt autem et Iudaei dicentes haec ita se habere
clem: Adjecerunt autem et Judi, dicentes hc ita se habere.
tr: συνεθεντο δε και οι ιουδαιοι φασκοντες ταυτα ουτως εχειν
kjv: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.

vulg: respondit autem Paulus annuente sibi praeside dicere ex multis annis esse te iudicem genti huic sciens bono animo pro me satisfaciam
clem: Respondit autem Paulus (annuente sibi prside dicere): Ex multis annis te esse judicem genti huic sciens, bono animo pro me satisfaciam.
tr: απεκριθη δε ο παυλος νευσαντος αυτω του ηγεμονος λεγειν εκ πολλων ετων οντα σε κριτην τω εθνει τουτω επισταμενος ευθυμοτερον τα περι εμαυτου απολογουμαι
kjv: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:

vulg: potes enim cognoscere quia non plus sunt dies mihi quam duodecim ex quo ascendi adorare in Hierusalem
clem: Potes enim cognoscere quia non plus sunt mihi dies quam duodecim, ex quo ascendi adorare in Jerusalem:
tr: δυναμενου σου γνωναι οτι ου πλειους εισιν μοι ημεραι η δεκαδυο αφ ης ανεβην προσκυνησων εν ιερουσαλημ
kjv: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.

vulg: et neque in templo invenerunt me cum aliquo disputantem aut concursum facientem turbae neque in synagogis neque in civitate
clem: et neque in templo invenerunt me cum aliquo disputantem, aut concursum facientem turb, neque in synagogis, neque in civitate:
tr: και ουτε εν τω ιερω ευρον με προς τινα διαλεγομενον η επισυστασιν ποιουντα οχλου ουτε εν ταις συναγωγαις ουτε κατα την πολιν
kjv: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:

vulg: neque probare possunt tibi de quibus nunc accusant me
clem: neque probare possunt tibi de quibus nunc me accusant.
tr: ουτε παραστησαι με   δυνανται περι ων νυν κατηγορουσιν μου
kjv: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.

vulg: confiteor autem hoc tibi quod secundum sectam quam dicunt heresim sic deservio patrio Deo meo credens omnibus quae in lege et prophetis scripta sunt
clem: Confiteor autem hoc tibi, quod secundum sectam quam dicunt hresim, sic deservio Patri et Deo meo, credens omnibus qu in lege et prophetis scripta sunt:
tr: ομολογω δε τουτο σοι οτι κατα την οδον ην λεγουσιν αιρεσιν ουτως λατρευω τω πατρωω θεω πιστευων πασιν τοις κατα τον νομον και τοις προφηταις γεγραμμενοις
kjv: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:

vulg: spem habens in Deum quam et hii ipsi expectant resurrectionem futuram iustorum et iniquorum
clem: spem habens in Deum, quam et hi ipsi exspectant, resurrectionem futuram justorum et iniquorum.
tr: ελπιδα εχων εις τον θεον ην και αυτοι ουτοι προσδεχονται αναστασιν μελλειν εσεσθαι νεκρων δικαιων τε και αδικων
kjv: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

vulg: in hoc et ipse studeo sine offendiculo conscientiam habere ad Deum et ad homines semper
clem: In hoc et ipse studeo sine offendiculo conscientiam habere ad Deum et ad homines semper.
tr: εν τουτω δε αυτος ασκω απροσκοπον συνειδησιν εχειν προς τον θεον και τους ανθρωπους διαπαντος  δια παντος
kjv: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void to offence toward God, and toward men.

vulg: post annos autem plures elemosynas facturus in gentem meam veni et oblationes et vota
clem: Post annos autem plures eleemosynas facturus in gentem meam, veni, et oblationes, et vota,
tr: δι ετων δε πλειονων παρεγενομην ελεημοσυνας ποιησων εις το εθνος μου και προσφορας
kjv: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.

vulg: in quibus invenerunt me purificatum in templo non cum turba neque cum tumultu
clem: in quibus invenerunt me purificatum in templo: non cum turba, neque cum tumultu.
tr: εν οις ευρον με ηγνισμενον εν τω ιερω ου μετα οχλου ουδε μετα θορυβου τινες δε   απο της ασιας ιουδαιοι
kjv: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.

vulg: quidam autem ex Asia Iudaei quos oportebat apud te praesto esse et accusare si quid haberent adversum me
clem: Quidam autem ex Asia Judi, quos oportebat apud te prsto esse, et accusare si quid haberent adversum me:
tr: ους δει  εδει  επι σου παρειναι και κατηγορειν ει τι εχοιεν προς με
kjv: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.

vulg: aut hii ipsi dicant si quid invenerunt in me iniquitatis cum stem in concilio
clem: aut hi ipsi dicant si quid invenerunt in me iniquitatis cum stem in concilio,
tr: η αυτοι ουτοι ειπατωσαν ει τι ευρον εν εμοι αδικημα σταντος μου επι του συνεδριου
kjv: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,

vulg: nisi de una hac solummodo voce qua clamavi inter eos stans quoniam de resurrectione mortuorum ego iudicor hodie a vobis
clem: nisi de una hac solummodo voce qua clamavi inter eos stans: Quoniam de resurrectione mortuorum ego judicor hodie a vobis.
tr: η περι μιας ταυτης φωνης ης εκραξα εστως εν αυτοις οτι περι αναστασεως νεκρων εγω κρινομαι σημερον υφ υμων
kjv: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.

vulg: distulit autem illos Felix certissime sciens de via dicens cum tribunus Lysias descenderit audiam vos
clem: Distulit autem illos Felix, certissime sciens de via hac, dicens: Cum tribunus Lysias descenderit, audiam vos.
tr: ακουσας δε ταυτα ο φηλιξ ανεβαλετο αυτους ακριβεστερον ειδως τα περι της οδου ειπων οταν λυσιας ο χιλιαρχος καταβη διαγνωσομαι τα καθ υμας
kjv: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.

vulg: iussitque centurioni custodiri eum et habere requiem nec quemquam prohibere de suis ministrare ei
clem: Jussitque centurioni custodire eum, et habere requiem, nec quemquam de suis prohibere ministrare ei.
tr: διαταξαμενος τε τω εκατονταρχη τηρεισθαι τον παυλον εχειν τε ανεσιν και μηδενα κωλυειν των ιδιων αυτου υπηρετειν η προσερχεσθαι αυτω
kjv: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.

vulg: post aliquot autem dies veniens Felix cum Drusilla uxore sua quae erat Iudaea vocavit Paulum et audivit ab eo fidem quae est in Iesum Christum
clem: Post aliquot autem dies veniens Felix cum Drusilla uxore sua, qu erat Juda, vocavit Paulum, et audivit ab eo fidem qu est in Christum Jesum.
tr: μετα δε ημερας τινας παραγενομενος ο φηλιξ συν δρουσιλλη τη γυναικι αυτου ουση ιουδαια μετεπεμψατο τον παυλον και ηκουσεν αυτου περι της εις χριστον πιστεως
kjv: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.

vulg: disputante autem illo de iustitia et castitate et de iudicio futuro timefactus Felix respondit quod nunc adtinet vade tempore autem oportuno accersiam te
clem: Disputante autem illo de justitia, et castitate, et de judicio futuro, tremefactus Felix, respondit: Quod nunc attinet, vade: tempore autem opportuno accersam te:
tr: διαλεγομενου δε αυτου περι δικαιοσυνης και εγκρατειας και του κριματος του μελλοντος εσεσθαι εμφοβος γενομενος ο φηλιξ απεκριθη το νυν εχον πορευου καιρον δε μεταλαβων μετακαλεσομαι σε
kjv: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.

vulg: simul et sperans quia pecunia daretur a Paulo propter quod et frequenter accersiens eum loquebatur cum eo
clem: simul et sperans quod pecunia ei daretur a Paulo, propter quod et frequenter accersens eum, loquebatur cum eo.
tr: αμα δε και ελπιζων οτι χρηματα δοθησεται αυτω υπο του παυλου οπως λυση αυτον διο και πυκνοτερον αυτον μεταπεμπομενος ωμιλει αυτω
kjv: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.

vulg: biennio autem expleto accepit successorem Felix Porcium Festum volens autem gratiam praestare Iudaeis Felix reliquit Paulum vinctum
clem: Biennio autem expleto, accepit successorem Felix Portium Festum. Volens autem gratiam prstare Judis Felix, reliquit Paulum vinctum.
tr: διετιας δε πληρωθεισης ελαβεν διαδοχον ο φηλιξ πορκιον φηστον θελων τε χαριτας καταθεσθαι τοις ιουδαιοις ο φηλιξ κατελιπεν τον παυλον δεδεμενον
kjv: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix' room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.

vulg: Festus ergo cum venisset in provinciam post triduum ascendit Hierosolymam a Caesarea
clem: Festus ergo cum venisset in provinciam, post triduum ascendit Jerosolymam a Csarea.
tr: φηστος ουν επιβας τη επαρχια μετα τρεις ημερας ανεβη εις ιεροσολυμα απο καισαρειας
kjv: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

vulg: adieruntque eum principes sacerdotum et primi Iudaeorum adversus Paulum et rogabant eum
clem: Adieruntque eum principes sacerdotum et primi Judorum adversus Paulum: et rogabant eum,
tr: ενεφανισαν δε αυτω ο αρχιερευς και οι πρωτοι των ιουδαιων κατα του παυλου και παρεκαλουν αυτον
kjv: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,

vulg: postulantes gratiam adversum eum ut iuberet perduci eum Hierusalem insidias tendentes ut eum interficerent in via
clem: postulantes gratiam adversus eum, ut juberet perduci eum in Jerusalem, insidias tendentes ut interficerent eum in via.
tr: αιτουμενοι χαριν κατ αυτου οπως μεταπεμψηται αυτον εις ιερουσαλημ ενεδραν ποιουντες ανελειν αυτον κατα την οδον
kjv: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.

vulg: Festus autem respondit servari Paulum in Caesarea se autem maturius profecturum
clem: Festus autem respondit servari Paulum in Csarea: se autem maturius profecturum.
tr: ο μεν ουν φηστος απεκριθη τηρεισθαι τον παυλον εν καισαρεια εαυτον δε μελλειν εν ταχει εκπορευεσθαι
kjv: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.

vulg: qui ergo in vobis ait potentes sunt descendentes simul si quod est in viro crimen accusent eum
clem: Qui ergo in vobis, ait, potentes sunt, descendentes simul, si quod est in viro crimen, accusent eum.
tr: οι ουν δυνατοι εν υμιν φησιν συγκαταβαντες ει τι εστιν  ατοπον  εν τω ανδρι τουτω κατηγορειτωσαν αυτου
kjv: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.

vulg: demoratus autem inter eos dies non amplius quam octo aut decem descendit Caesaream et altera die sedit pro tribunali et iussit Paulum adduci
clem: Demoratus autem inter eos dies non amplius quam octo aut decem, descendit Csaream, et altera die sedit pro tribunali, et jussit Paulum adduci.
tr: διατριψας δε εν αυτοις ημερας πλειους η δεκα καταβας εις καισαρειαν τη επαυριον καθισας επι του βηματος εκελευσεν τον παυλον αχθηναι
kjv: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Caesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.

vulg: qui cum perductus esset circumsteterunt eum qui ab Hierosolyma descenderant Iudaei multas et graves causas obicientes quas non poterant probare
clem: Qui cum perductus esset, circumsteterunt eum, qui ab Jerosolyma descenderant Judi, multas et graves causas objicientes, quas non poterant probare:
tr: παραγενομενου δε αυτου περιεστησαν οι απο ιεροσολυμων καταβεβηκοτες ιουδαιοι πολλα και βαρεα αιτιαματα φεροντες κατα του παυλου α ουκ ισχυον αποδειξαι
kjv: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.

vulg: Paulo autem rationem reddente quoniam neque in legem Iudaeorum neque in templum neque in Caesarem quicquam peccavi
clem: Paulo rationem reddente: Quoniam neque in legem Judorum, neque in templum, neque in Csarem quidquam peccavi.
tr: απολογουμενου αυτου οτι ουτε εις τον νομον των ιουδαιων ουτε εις το ιερον ουτε εις καισαρα τι ημαρτον
kjv: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar, have I offended any thing at all.

vulg: Festus autem volens Iudaeis gratiam praestare respondens Paulo dixit vis Hierosolymam ascendere et ibi de his iudicari apud me
clem: Festus autem volens gratiam prstare Judis, respondens Paulo, dixit: Vis Jerosolymam ascendere, et ibi de his judicari apud me?
tr: ο φηστος δε τοις ιουδαιοις θελων χαριν καταθεσθαι αποκριθεις τω παυλω ειπεν θελεις εις ιεροσολυμα αναβας εκει περι τουτων κρινεσθαι επ εμου
kjv: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?

vulg: dixit autem Paulus ad tribunal Caesaris sto ubi me oportet iudicari Iudaeis non nocui sicut tu melius nosti
clem: Dixit autem Paulus: Ad tribunal Csaris sto: ibi me oportet judicari: Judis non nocui, sicut tu melius nosti.
tr: ειπεν δε ο παυλος επι του βηματος καισαρος εστως ειμι ου με δει κρινεσθαι ιουδαιους ουδεν ηδικησα ως και συ καλλιον επιγινωσκεις
kjv: Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.

vulg: si enim nocui aut dignum morte aliquid feci non recuso mori si vero nihil est eorum quae hii accusant me nemo potest me illis donare Caesarem appello
clem: Si enim nocui, aut dignum morte aliquid feci, non recuso mori: si vero nihil est eorum qu hi accusant me, nemo potest me illis donare. Csarem appello.
tr: ει μεν γαρ αδικω και αξιον θανατου πεπραχα τι ου παραιτουμαι το αποθανειν ει δε ουδεν εστιν ων ουτοι κατηγορουσιν μου ουδεις με δυναται αυτοις χαρισασθαι καισαρα επικαλουμαι
kjv: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar.

vulg: tunc Festus cum consilio locutus respondit Caesarem appellasti ad Caesarem ibis
clem: Tunc Festus cum concilio locutus, respondit: Csarem appellasti? ad Csarem ibis.
tr: τοτε ο φηστος συλλαλησας μετα του συμβουλιου απεκριθη καισαρα επικεκλησαι επι καισαρα πορευση
kjv: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Caesar? unto Caesar shalt thou go.

vulg: et cum dies aliquot transacti essent Agrippa rex et Bernice descenderunt Caesaream ad salutandum Festum
clem: Et cum dies aliquot transacti essent, Agrippa rex et Bernice descenderunt Csaream ad salutandum Festum.
tr: ημερων δε διαγενομενων τινων αγριππας ο βασιλευς και βερνικη κατηντησαν εις καισαρειαν ασπασομενοι τον φηστον
kjv: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus.

vulg: et cum dies plures ibi demorarentur Festus regi indicavit de Paulo dicens vir quidam est derelictus a Felice vinctus
clem: Et cum dies plures ibi demorarentur, Festus regi indicavit de Paulo, dicens: Vir quidam est derelictus a Felice vinctus,
tr: ως δε πλειους ημερας διετριβον εκει ο φηστος τω βασιλει ανεθετο τα κατα τον παυλον λεγων ανηρ τις εστιν καταλελειμμενος υπο φηλικος δεσμιος
kjv: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul's cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:

vulg: de quo cum essem Hierosolymis adierunt me principes sacerdotum et seniores Iudaeorum postulantes adversus illum damnationem
clem: de quo cum essem Jerosolymis, adierunt me principes sacerdotum et seniores Judorum, postulantes adversus illum damnationem.
tr: περι ου γενομενου μου εις ιεροσολυμα ενεφανισαν οι αρχιερεις και οι πρεσβυτεροι των ιουδαιων αιτουμενοι κατ αυτου δικην
kjv: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, desiring to have judgment against him.

vulg: ad quos respondi quia non est consuetudo Romanis donare aliquem hominem priusquam is qui accusatur praesentes habeat accusatores locumque defendendi accipiat ad abluenda crimina
clem: Ad quos respondi: Quia non est Romanis consuetudo damnare aliquem hominem priusquam is qui accusatur prsentes habeat accusatores, locumque defendendi accipiat ad abluenda crimina.
tr: προς ους απεκριθην οτι ουκ εστιν εθος ρωμαιοις χαριζεσθαι τινα ανθρωπον εις απωλειαν πριν η ο κατηγορουμενος κατα προσωπον εχοι τους κατηγορους τοπον τε απολογιας λαβοι περι του εγκληματος
kjv: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.

vulg: cum ergo huc convenissent sine ulla dilatione sequenti die sedens pro tribunali iussi adduci virum
clem: Cum ergo huc convenissent sine ulla dilatione, sequenti die sedens pro tribunali, jussi adduci virum.
tr: συνελθοντων ουν αυτων ενθαδε αναβολην μηδεμιαν ποιησαμενος τη εξης καθισας επι του βηματος εκελευσα αχθηναι τον ανδρα
kjv: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.

vulg: de quo cum stetissent accusatores nullam causam deferebant de quibus ego suspicabar malum
clem: De quo, cum stetissent accusatores, nullam causam deferebant, de quibus ego suspicabar malum.
tr: περι ου σταθεντες οι κατηγοροι ουδεμιαν αιτιαν επεφερον ων υπενοουν εγω
kjv: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:

vulg: quaestiones vero quasdam de sua superstitione habebant adversus eum et de quodam Iesu defuncto quem adfirmabat Paulus vivere
clem: Qustiones vero quasdam de sua superstitione habebant adversus eum, et de quodam Jesu defuncto, quem affirmabat Paulus vivere.
tr: ζητηματα δε τινα περι της ιδιας δεισιδαιμονιας ειχον προς αυτον και περι τινος ιησου τεθνηκοτος ον εφασκεν ο παυλος ζην
kjv: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

vulg: haesitans autem ego de huiusmodi quaestione dicebam si vellet ire Hierosolymam et ibi iudicari de istis
clem: Hsitans autem ego de hujusmodi qustione, dicebam si vellet ire Jerosolymam, et ibi judicari de istis.
tr: απορουμενος δε εγω εις την περι τουτου ζητησιν ελεγον ει βουλοιτο πορευεσθαι εις ιερουσαλημ κακει κρινεσθαι περι τουτων
kjv: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.

vulg: Paulo autem appellante ut servaretur ad Augusti cognitionem iussi servari eum donec mittam eum ad Caesarem
clem: Paulo autem appellante ut servaretur ad Augusti cognitionem, jussi servari eum, donec mittam eum ad Csarem.
tr: του δε παυλου επικαλεσαμενου τηρηθηναι αυτον εις την του σεβαστου διαγνωσιν εκελευσα τηρεισθαι αυτον εως ου πεμψω αυτον προς καισαρα
kjv: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.

vulg: Agrippa autem ad Festum volebam et ipse hominem audire cras inquit audies eum
clem: Agrippa autem dixit ad Festum: Volebam et ipse hominem audire. Cras, inquit, audies eum.
tr: αγριππας δε προς τον φηστον εφη εβουλομην και αυτος του ανθρωπου ακουσαι ο δε αυριον φησιν ακουση αυτου
kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.

vulg: altera autem die cum venisset Agrippa et Bernice cum multa ambitione et introissent in auditorium cum tribunis et viris principalibus civitatis et iubente Festo adductus est Paulus
clem: Altera autem die cum venisset Agrippa et Bernice cum multa ambitione, et introissent in auditorium cum tribunis et viris principalibus civitatis, jubente Festo, adductus est Paulus.
tr: τη ουν επαυριον ελθοντος του αγριππα και της βερνικης μετα πολλης φαντασιας και εισελθοντων εις το ακροατηριον συν τε τοις χιλιαρχοις και ανδρασιν τοις κατ εξοχην ουσιν της πολεως και κελευσαντος του φηστου ηχθη ο παυλος
kjv: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus' commandment Paul was brought forth.

vulg: et dixit Festus Agrippa rex et omnes qui simul adestis nobiscum viri videtis hunc de quo omnis multitudo Iudaeorum interpellavit me Hierosolymis petens et hic clamantes non oportere eum vivere amplius
clem: Et dicit Festus: Agrippa rex, et omnes qui simul adestis nobiscum viri, videtis hunc de quo omnis multitudo Judorum interpellavit me Jerosolymis, petentes et acclamantes non oportere eum vivere amplius.
tr: και φησιν ο φηστος αγριππα βασιλευ και παντες οι συμπαροντες ημιν ανδρες θεωρειτε τουτον περι ου παν το πληθος των ιουδαιων ενετυχον μοι εν τε ιεροσολυμοις και ενθαδε επιβοωντες μη δειν ζην αυτον μηκετι
kjv: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

vulg: ego vero conperi nihil dignum eum morte admisisse ipso autem hoc appellante Augustum iudicavi mittere
clem: Ego vere comperi nihil dignum morte eum admisisse. Ipso autem hoc appellante ad Augustum, judicavi mittere.
tr: εγω δε καταλαβομενος μηδεν αξιον θανατου αυτον πεπραχεναι και αυτου δε τουτου επικαλεσαμενου τον σεβαστον εκρινα πεμπειν αυτον
kjv: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.

vulg: de quo quid certum scribam domino non habeo propter quod produxi eum ad vos et maxime ad te rex Agrippa ut interrogatione facta habeam quid scribam
clem: De quo quid certum scribam domino, non habeo. Propter quod produxi eum ad vos, et maxime ad te, rex Agrippa, ut interrogatione facta habeam quid scribam.
tr: περι ου ασφαλες τι γραψαι τω κυριω ουκ εχω διο προηγαγον αυτον εφ υμων και μαλιστα επι σου βασιλευ αγριππα οπως της ανακρισεως γενομενης σχω τι γραψαι
kjv: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.

vulg: sine ratione enim mihi videtur mittere vinctum et causas eius non significare
clem: Sine ratione enim mihi videtur mittere vinctum, et causas ejus non significare.
tr: αλογον γαρ μοι δοκει πεμποντα δεσμιον μη και τας κατ αυτου αιτιας σημαναι
kjv: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.

vulg: Agrippa vero ad Paulum ait permittitur tibi loqui pro temet ipso tunc Paulus extenta manu coepit rationem reddere
clem: Agrippa vero ad Paulum ait: Permittitur tibi loqui pro temetipso. Tunc Paulus extenta manu cpit rationem reddere:
tr: αγριππας δε προς τον παυλον εφη επιτρεπεται σοι υπερ σεαυτου λεγειν τοτε ο παυλος απελογειτο εκτεινας την χειρα
kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:

vulg: de omnibus quibus accusor a Iudaeis rex Agrippa aestimo me beatum apud te cum sim defensurus me hodie
clem: De omnibus quibus accusor a Judis, rex Agrippa, stimo me beatum apud te cum sim defensurus me hodie,
tr: περι παντων ων εγκαλουμαι υπο ιουδαιων βασιλευ αγριππα ηγημαι εμαυτον μακαριον μελλων απολογεισθαι επι σου σημερον
kjv: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:

vulg: maxime te sciente omnia quae apud Iudaeos sunt consuetudines et quaestiones propter quod obsecro patienter me audias
clem: maxime te sciente omnia, et qu apud Judos sunt consuetudines et qustiones: propter quod obsecro patienter me audias.
tr: μαλιστα γνωστην οντα σε  ειδως  παντων των κατα ιουδαιους εθων τε και ζητηματων διο δεομαι σου μακροθυμως ακουσαι μου
kjv: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.

vulg: et quidem vitam meam a iuventute quae ab initio fuit in gente mea in Hierosolymis noverunt omnes Iudaei
clem: Et quidem vitam meam a juventute, qu ab initio fuit in gente mea in Jerosolymis, noverunt omnes Judi:
tr: την μεν ουν βιωσιν μου την εκ νεοτητος την απ αρχης γενομενην εν τω εθνει μου εν ιεροσολυμοις ισασιν παντες οι ιουδαιοι
kjv: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;

vulg: praescientes me ab initio si velint testimonium perhibere quoniam secundum certissimam sectam nostrae religionis vixi Pharisaeus
clem: prscientes me ab initio (si velint testimonium perhibere) quoniam secundum certissimam sectam nostr religionis vixi pharisus.
tr: προγινωσκοντες με ανωθεν εαν θελωσιν μαρτυρειν οτι κατα την ακριβεστατην αιρεσιν της ημετερας θρησκειας εζησα φαρισαιος
kjv: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

vulg: et nunc in spe quae ad patres nostros repromissionis facta est a Deo sto iudicio subiectus
clem: Et nunc, in spe qu ad patres nostros repromissionis facta est a Deo, sto judicio subjectus:
tr: και νυν επ ελπιδι της προς τους πατερας επαγγελιας γενομενης υπο του θεου εστηκα κρινομενος
kjv: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God, unto our fathers:

vulg: in quam duodecim tribus nostrae nocte ac die deservientes sperant devenire de qua spe accusor a Iudaeis rex
clem: in quam duodecim tribus nostr nocte ac die deservientes, sperant devenire. De qua spe accusor a Judis, rex.
tr: εις ην το δωδεκαφυλον ημων εν εκτενεια νυκτα και ημεραν λατρευον ελπιζει καταντησαι περι ης ελπιδος εγκαλουμαι βασιλευ αγριππα υπο των ιουδαιων
kjv: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope's sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.

vulg: quid incredibile iudicatur apud vos si Deus mortuos suscitat
clem: Quid incredibile judicatur apud vos, si Deus mortuos suscitat?
tr: τι απιστον κρινεται παρ υμιν ει ο θεος νεκρους εγειρει
kjv: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?

vulg: et ego quidem existimaveram me adversus nomen Iesu Nazareni debere multa contraria agere
clem: Et ego quidem existimaveram me adversus nomen Jesu Nazareni debere multa contraria agere,
tr: εγω μεν ουν εδοξα εμαυτω προς το ονομα ιησου του ναζωραιου δειν πολλα εναντια πραξαι
kjv: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

vulg: quod et feci Hierosolymis et multos sanctorum ego in carceribus inclusi a principibus sacerdotum potestate accepta et cum occiderentur detuli sententiam
clem: quod et feci Jerosolymis, et multos sanctorum ego in carceribus inclusi, a principibus sacerdotum potestate accepta: et cum occiderentur, detuli sententiam.
tr: ο και εποιησα εν ιεροσολυμοις και πολλους των αγιων εγω φυλακαις κατεκλεισα την παρα των αρχιερεων εξουσιαν λαβων αναιρουμενων τε αυτων κατηνεγκα ψηφον
kjv: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.

vulg: et per omnes synagogas frequenter puniens eos conpellebam blasphemare et amplius insaniens in eos persequebar usque in exteras civitates
clem: Et per omnes synagogas frequenter puniens eos, compellebam blasphemare: et amplius insaniens in eos, persequebar usque in exteras civitates.
tr: και κατα πασας τας συναγωγας πολλακις τιμωρων αυτους ηναγκαζον βλασφημειν περισσως τε εμμαινομενος αυτοις εδιωκον εως και εις τας εξω πολεις
kjv: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.

vulg: in quibus dum irem Damascum cum potestate et permissu principum sacerdotum
clem: In quibus dum irem Damascum cum potestate et permissu principum sacerdotum,
tr: εν οις και πορευομενος εις την δαμασκον μετ εξουσιας και επιτροπης της παρα των αρχιερεων
kjv: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,

vulg: die media in via vidi rex de caelo supra splendorem solis circumfulsisse me lumen et eos qui mecum simul erant
clem: die media in via vidi, rex, de clo supra splendorem solis circumfulsisse me lumen, et eos qui mecum simul erant.
tr: ημερας μεσης κατα την οδον ειδον βασιλευ ουρανοθεν υπερ την λαμπροτητα του ηλιου περιλαμψαν με φως και τους συν εμοι πορευομενους
kjv: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.

vulg: omnesque nos cum decidissemus in terram audivi vocem loquentem mihi hebraica lingua Saule Saule quid me persequeris durum est tibi contra stimulum calcitrare
clem: Omnesque nos cum decidissemus in terram, audivi vocem loquentem mihi hebraica lingua: Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris? durum est tibi contra stimulum calcitrare.
tr: παντων δε καταπεσοντων ημων εις την γην ηκουσα φωνην λαλουσαν προς με και λεγουσαν τη εβραιδι διαλεκτω σαουλ σαουλ τι με διωκεις σκληρον σοι προς κεντρα λακτιζειν
kjv: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

vulg: ego autem dixi quis es Domine Dominus autem dixit ego sum Iesus quem tu persequeris
clem: Ego autem dixi: Quis es, domine? Dominus autem dixit: Ego sum Jesus, quem tu persequeris.
tr: εγω δε ειπον τις ει κυριε ο δε ειπεν εγω ειμι ιησους ον συ διωκεις
kjv: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.

vulg: sed exsurge et sta super pedes tuos ad hoc enim apparui tibi ut constituam te ministrum et testem eorum quae vidisti et eorum quibus apparebo tibi
clem: Sed exsurge, et sta super pedes tuos: ad hoc enim apparui tibi, ut constituam te ministrum, et testem eorum qu vidisti, et eorum quibus apparebo tibi,
tr: αλλα αναστηθι και στηθι επι τους ποδας σου εις τουτο γαρ ωφθην σοι προχειρισασθαι σε υπηρετην και μαρτυρα ων τε ειδες ων τε οφθησομαι σοι
kjv: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;

vulg: eripiens te de populo et gentibus in quas nunc ego mitto te
clem: eripiens te de populo et gentibus, in quas nunc ego mitto te,
tr: εξαιρουμενος σε εκ του λαου και των εθνων εις ους νυν σε αποστελλω
kjv: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,

vulg: aperire oculos eorum ut convertantur a tenebris ad lucem et de potestate Satanae ad Deum ut accipiant remissionem peccatorum et sortem inter sanctos per fidem quae est in me
clem: aperire oculos eorum, ut convertantur a tenebris ad lucem, et de potestate Satan ad Deum, ut accipiant remissionem peccatorum, et sortem inter sanctos, per fidem qu est in me.
tr: ανοιξαι οφθαλμους αυτων του  και  επιστρεψαι απο σκοτους εις φως και της εξουσιας του σατανα επι τον θεον του λαβειν αυτους αφεσιν αμαρτιων και κληρον εν τοις ηγιασμενοις πιστει τη εις εμε
kjv: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.

vulg: unde rex Agrippa non fui incredulus caelestis visionis
clem: Unde, rex Agrippa, non fui incredulus clesti visioni:
tr: οθεν βασιλευ αγριππα ουκ εγενομην απειθης τη ουρανιω οπτασια
kjv: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:

vulg: sed his qui sunt Damasci primum et Hierosolymis et in omnem regionem Iudaeae et gentibus adnuntiabam ut paenitentiam agerent et converterentur ad Deum digna paenitentiae opera facientes
clem: sed his qui sunt Damasci primum, et Jerosolymis, et in omnem regionem Jud, et gentibus, annuntiabam, ut pnitentiam agerent, et converterentur ad Deum, digna pnitenti opera facientes.
tr: αλλα τοις εν δαμασκω πρωτον και ιεροσολυμοις εις πασαν τε την χωραν της ιουδαιας και τοις εθνεσιν απαγγελλων  απηγγελλον  μετανοειν και επιστρεφειν επι τον θεον αξια της μετανοιας εργα πρασσοντας
kjv: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.

vulg: hac ex causa me Iudaei cum essem in templo conprehensum temptabant interficere
clem: Hac ex causa me Judi, cum essem in templo, comprehensum tentabant interficere.
tr: ενεκα τουτων με οι ιουδαιοι συλλαβομενοι εν τω ιερω επειρωντο διαχειρισασθαι
kjv: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.

vulg: auxilio autem adiutus Dei usque in hodiernum diem sto testificans minori atque maiori nihil extra dicens quam ea quae prophetae sunt locuti futura esse et Moses
clem: Auxilio autem adjutus Dei usque in hodiernum diem, sto, testificans minori atque majori, nihil extra dicens quam ea qu prophet locuti sunt futura esse, et Moyses,
tr: επικουριας ουν τυχων της παρα του θεου αχρι της ημερας ταυτης εστηκα μαρτυρουμενος μικρω τε και μεγαλω ουδεν εκτος λεγων ων τε οι προφηται ελαλησαν μελλοντων γινεσθαι και μωσης
kjv: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:

vulg: si passibilis Christus si primus ex resurrectione mortuorum lumen adnuntiaturus est populo et gentibus
clem: si passibilis Christus, si primus ex resurrectione mortuorum, lumen annuntiaturus est populo et gentibus.
tr: ει παθητος ο χριστος ει πρωτος εξ αναστασεως νεκρων φως μελλει καταγγελλειν τω λαω και τοις εθνεσιν
kjv: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.

vulg: haec loquente eo et rationem reddente Festus magna voce dixit insanis Paule multae te litterae ad insaniam convertunt
clem: Hc loquente eo, et rationem reddente, Festus magna voce dixit: Insanis, Paule: mult te litter ad insaniam convertunt.
tr: ταυτα δε αυτου απολογουμενου ο φηστος μεγαλη τη φωνη εφη μαινη παυλε τα πολλα σε γραμματα εις μανιαν περιτρεπει
kjv: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.

vulg: at Paulus non insanio inquit optime Feste sed veritatis et sobrietatis verba eloquor
clem: Et Paulus: Non insanio, inquit, optime Feste, sed veritatis et sobrietatis verba loquor.
tr: ο δε ου μαινομαι φησιν κρατιστε φηστε αλλ αληθειας και σωφροσυνης ρηματα αποφθεγγομαι
kjv: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.

vulg: scit enim de his rex ad quem et constanter loquor latere enim eum nihil horum arbitror neque enim in angulo quicquam horum gestum est
clem: Scit enim de his rex, ad quem et constanter loquor: latere enim eum nihil horum arbitror. Neque enim in angulo quidquam horum gestum est.
tr: επισταται γαρ περι τουτων ο βασιλευς προς ον και παρρησιαζομενος λαλω λανθανειν γαρ αυτον τι τουτων ου πειθομαι ουδεν ου γαρ εστιν εν γωνια πεπραγμενον τουτο
kjv: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.

vulg: credis rex Agrippa prophetis scio quia credis
clem: Credis, rex Agrippa, prophetis? Scio quia credis.
tr: πιστευεις βασιλευ αγριππα τοις προφηταις οιδα οτι πιστευεις
kjv: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.

vulg: Agrippa autem ad Paulum in modico suades me Christianum fieri
clem: Agrippa autem ad Paulum: In modico suades me christianum fieri.
tr: ο δε αγριππας προς τον παυλον εφη εν ολιγω με πειθεις χριστιανον γενεσθαι
kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.

vulg: et Paulus opto apud Deum et in modico et in magno non tantum te sed et omnes hos qui audiunt hodie fieri tales qualis et ego sum exceptis vinculis his
clem: Et Paulus: Opto apud Deum, et in modico et in magno, non tantum te, sed etiam omnes qui audiunt hodie fieri tales, qualis et ego sum, exceptis vinculis his.
tr: ο δε παυλος ειπεν ευξαιμην αν τω θεω και εν ολιγω και εν πολλω ου μονον σε αλλα και παντας τους ακουοντας μου σημερον γενεσθαι τοιουτους οποιος καγω ειμι παρεκτος των δεσμων τουτων
kjv: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.

vulg: et exsurrexit rex et praeses et Bernice et qui adsidebant eis
clem: Et exsurrexit rex, et prses, et Bernice, et qui assidebant eis.
tr: και ταυτα ειποντος αυτου ανεστη ο βασιλευς και ο ηγεμων η τε βερνικη και οι συγκαθημενοι αυτοις
kjv: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:

vulg: et cum secessissent loquebantur ad invicem dicentes quia nihil morte aut vinculorum dignum quid facit homo iste
clem: Et cum secessissent, loquebantur ad invicem, dicentes: Quia nihil morte aut vinculis dignum quid fecit homo iste.
tr: και αναχωρησαντες ελαλουν προς αλληλους λεγοντες οτι ουδεν θανατου αξιον η δεσμων πρασσει ο ανθρωπος ουτος
kjv: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

vulg: Agrippa autem Festo dixit dimitti poterat homo hic si non appellasset Caesarem
clem: Agrippa autem Festo dixit: Dimitti poterat homo hic, si non appellasset Csarem.
tr: αγριππας δε τω φηστω εφη απολελυσθαι εδυνατο ο ανθρωπος ουτος ει μη επεκεκλητο καισαρα
kjv: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.

vulg: ut autem iudicatum est eum navigare in Italiam et tradi Paulum cum reliquis custodiis centurioni nomine Iulio cohortis Augustae
clem: Ut autem judicatum est navigare eum in Italiam, et tradi Paulum cum reliquis custodiis centurioni nomine Julio cohortis August,
tr: ως δε εκριθη του αποπλειν ημας εις την ιταλιαν παρεδιδουν τον τε παυλον και τινας ετερους δεσμωτας εκατονταρχη ονοματι ιουλιω σπειρης σεβαστης
kjv: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band.

vulg: ascendentes autem navem hadrumetinam incipientem navigare circa Asiae loca sustulimus perseverante nobiscum Aristarcho Macedone Thessalonicense
clem: ascendentes navem Adrumetinam, incipientes navigare circa Asi loca, sustulimus, perseverante nobiscum Aristarcho Macedone Thessalonicensi.
tr: επιβαντες δε πλοιω αδραμυττηνω μελλοντες πλειν τους κατα την ασιαν τοπους ανηχθημεν οντος συν ημιν αρισταρχου μακεδονος θεσσαλονικεως
kjv: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

vulg: sequenti autem die devenimus Sidonem humane autem tractans Iulius Paulum permisit ad amicos ire et curam sui agere
clem: Sequenti autem die devenimus Sidonem. Humane autem tractans Julius Paulum, permisit ad amicos ire, et curam sui agere.
tr: τη τε ετερα κατηχθημεν εις σιδωνα φιλανθρωπως τε ο ιουλιος τω παυλω χρησαμενος επετρεψεν προς  τους  φιλους πορευθεντα επιμελειας τυχειν
kjv: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.

vulg: et inde cum sustulissemus subnavigavimus Cypro propterea quod essent venti contrarii
clem: Et inde cum sustulissemus, subnavigavimus Cyprum, propterea quod essent venti contrarii.
tr: κακειθεν αναχθεντες υπεπλευσαμεν την κυπρον δια το τους ανεμους ειναι εναντιους
kjv: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

vulg: et pelagus Ciliciae et Pamphiliae navigantes venimus Lystram quae est Lyciae
clem: Et pelagus Cilici et Pamphyli navigantes, venimus Lystram, qu est Lyci:
tr: το τε πελαγος το κατα την κιλικιαν και παμφυλιαν διαπλευσαντες κατηλθομεν εις μυρα της λυκιας
kjv: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

vulg: et ibi inveniens centurio navem alexandrinam navigantem in Italiam transposuit nos in eam
clem: et ibi inveniens centurio navem Alexandrinam navigantem in Italiam, transposuit nos in eam.
tr: κακει ευρων ο εκατονταρχος πλοιον αλεξανδρινον πλεον εις την ιταλιαν ενεβιβασεν ημας εις αυτο
kjv: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.

vulg: et cum multis diebus tarde navigaremus et vix devenissemus contra Cnidum prohibente nos vento adnavigavimus Cretae secundum Salmonem
clem: Et cum multis diebus tarde navigaremus, et vix devenissemus contra Gnidum, prohibente nos vento, adnavigavimus Cret juxta Salmonem:
tr: εν ικαναις δε ημεραις βραδυπλοουντες και μολις γενομενοι κατα την κνιδον μη προσεωντος ημας του ανεμου υπεπλευσαμεν την κρητην κατα σαλμωνην
kjv: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;

vulg: et vix iuxta navigantes venimus in locum quendam qui vocatur Boni portus cui iuxta erat civitas Thalassa
clem: et vix juxta navigantes, venimus in locum quemdam qui vocatur Boniportus, cui juxta erat civitas Thalassa.
tr: μολις τε παραλεγομενοι αυτην ηλθομεν εις τοπον τινα καλουμενον καλους λιμενας ω εγγυς ην πολις λασαια
kjv: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.

vulg: multo autem tempore peracto et cum iam non esset tuta navigatio eo quod et ieiunium iam praeterisset consolabatur Paulus
clem: Multo autem tempore peracto, et cum jam non esset tuta navigatio eo quod et jejunium jam prteriisset, consolabatur eos Paulus,
tr: ικανου δε χρονου διαγενομενου και οντος ηδη επισφαλους του πλοος δια το και την νηστειαν ηδη παρεληλυθεναι παρηνει ο παυλος
kjv: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,

vulg: dicens eis viri video quoniam cum iniuria et multo damno non solum oneris et navis sed etiam animarum nostrarum incipit esse navigatio
clem: dicens eis: Viri, video quoniam cum injuria et multo damno non solum oneris, et navis, sed etiam animarum nostrarum incipit esse navigatio.
tr: λεγων αυτοις ανδρες θεωρω οτι μετα υβρεως και πολλης ζημιας ου μονον του φορτου και του πλοιου αλλα και των ψυχων ημων μελλειν εσεσθαι τον πλουν
kjv: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.

vulg: centurio autem gubernatori et nauclerio magis credebat quam his quae a Paulo dicebantur
clem: Centurio autem gubernatori et nauclero magis credebat, quam his qu a Paulo dicebantur.
tr: ο δε εκατονταρχος τω κυβερνητη και τω ναυκληρω επειθετο μαλλον η τοις υπο του παυλου λεγομενοις
kjv: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.

vulg: et cum aptus portus non esset ad hiemandum plurimi statuerunt consilium navigare inde si quo modo possent devenientes Phoenice hiemare portum Cretae respicientem ad africum et ad chorum
clem: Et cum aptus portus non esset ad hiemandum, plurimi statuerunt consilium navigare inde, si quomodo possent, devenientes Phnicen hiemare, portum Cret respicientem ad Africum et ad Corum.
tr: ανευθετου δε του λιμενος υπαρχοντος προς παραχειμασιαν οι πλειους εθεντο βουλην αναχθηναι κακειθεν ειπως δυναιντο καταντησαντες εις φοινικα παραχειμασαι λιμενα της κρητης βλεποντα κατα λιβα και κατα χωρον
kjv: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.

vulg: adspirante autem austro aestimantes propositum se tenere cum sustulissent de Asson legebant Cretam
clem: Aspirante autem austro, stimantes propositum se tenere, cum sustulissent de Asson, legebant Cretam.
tr: υποπνευσαντος δε νοτου δοξαντες της προθεσεως κεκρατηκεναι αραντες ασσον παρελεγοντο την κρητην
kjv: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.

vulg: non post multum autem misit se contra ipsam ventus typhonicus qui vocatur euroaquilo
clem: Non post multum autem misit se contra ipsam ventus typhonicus, qui vocatur Euroaquilo.
tr: μετ ου πολυ δε εβαλεν κατ αυτης ανεμος τυφωνικος ο καλουμενος ευροκλυδων
kjv: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.

vulg: cumque arrepta esset navis et non posset conari in ventum data nave flatibus ferebamur
clem: Cumque arrepta esset navis, et non posset conari in ventum, data nave flatibus, ferebamur.
tr: συναρπασθεντος δε του πλοιου και μη δυναμενου αντοφθαλμειν τω ανεμω επιδοντες εφερομεθα
kjv: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.

vulg: insulam autem quandam decurrentes quae vocatur Caudam potuimus vix obtinere scapham
clem: In insulam autem quamdam decurrentes, qu vocatur Cauda, potuimus vix obtinere scapham.
tr: νησιον δε τι υποδραμοντες καλουμενον κλαυδην μολις ισχυσαμεν περικρατεις γενεσθαι της σκαφης
kjv: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:

vulg: qua sublata adiutoriis utebantur accingentes navem timentes ne in Syrtim inciderent submisso vase sic ferebantur
clem: Qua sublata, adjutoriis utebantur, accingentes navem, timentes ne in Syrtim inciderent, summisso vase sic ferebantur.
tr: ην αραντες βοηθειαις εχρωντο υποζωννυντες το πλοιον φοβουμενοι τε μη εις την συρτιν εκπεσωσιν χαλασαντες το σκευος ουτως εφεροντο
kjv: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.

vulg: valide autem nobis tempestate iactatis sequenti die iactum fecerunt
clem: Valida autem nobis tempestate jactatis, sequenti die jactum fecerunt:
tr: σφοδρως δε χειμαζομενων ημων τη εξης εκβολην εποιουντο
kjv: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;

vulg: et tertia die suis manibus armamenta navis proiecerunt
clem: et tertia die suis manibus armamenta navis projecerunt.
tr: και τη τριτη αυτοχειρες την σκευην του πλοιου ερριψαμεν
kjv: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.

vulg: neque sole autem neque sideribus apparentibus per plures dies et tempestate non exigua inminente iam ablata erat spes omnis salutis nostrae
clem: Neque autem sole, neque sideribus apparentibus per plures dies, et tempestate non exigua imminente, jam ablata erat spes omnis salutis nostr.
tr: μητε δε ηλιου μητε αστρων επιφαινοντων επι πλειονας ημερας χειμωνος τε ουκ ολιγου επικειμενου λοιπον περιηρειτο πασα ελπις του σωζεσθαι ημας
kjv: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.

vulg: et cum multa ieiunatio fuisset tunc stans Paulus in medio eorum dixit oportebat quidem o viri audito me non tollere a Creta lucrique facere iniuriam hanc et iacturam
clem: Et cum multa jejunatio fuisset, tunc stans Paulus in medio eorum, dixit: Oportebat quidem, o viri, audito me, non tollere a Creta, lucrique facere injuriam hanc et jacturam.
tr: πολλης δε ασιτιας υπαρχουσης τοτε σταθεις ο παυλος εν μεσω αυτων ειπεν εδει μεν ω ανδρες πειθαρχησαντας μοι μη αναγεσθαι απο της κρητης κερδησαι τε την υβριν ταυτην και την ζημιαν
kjv: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.

vulg: et nunc suadeo vobis bono animo esse amissio enim nullius animae erit ex vobis praeterquam navis
clem: Et nunc suadeo vobis bono animo esse: amissio enim nullius anim erit ex vobis, prterquam navis.
tr: και τανυν  τα νυν  παραινω υμας ευθυμειν αποβολη γαρ ψυχης ουδεμια εσται εξ υμων πλην του πλοιου
kjv: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship.

vulg: adstitit enim mihi hac nocte angelus Dei cuius sum ego et cui deservio
clem: Astitit enim mihi hac nocte angelus Dei, cujus sum ego, et cui deservio,
tr: παρεστη γαρ μοι τη νυκτι ταυτη αγγελος του θεου ου ειμι ω και λατρευω
kjv: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,

vulg: dicens ne timeas Paule Caesari te oportet adsistere et ecce donavit tibi Deus omnes qui navigant tecum
clem: dicens: Ne timeas, Paule: Csari te oportet assistere: et ecce donavit tibi Deus omnes qui navigant tecum.
tr: λεγων μη φοβου παυλε καισαρι σε δει παραστηναι και ιδου κεχαρισται σοι ο θεος παντας τους πλεοντας μετα σου
kjv: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

vulg: propter quod bono animo estote viri credo enim Deo quia sic erit quemadmodum dictum est mihi
clem: Propter quod bono animo estote, viri: credo enim Deo quia sic erit, quemadmodum dictum est mihi.
tr: διο ευθυμειτε ανδρες πιστευω γαρ τω θεω οτι ουτως εσται καθ ον τροπον λελαληται μοι
kjv: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.

vulg: in insulam autem quandam oportet nos devenire
clem: In insulam autem quamdam oportet nos devenire.
tr: εις νησον δε τινα δει ημας εκπεσειν
kjv: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.

vulg: sed posteaquam quartadecima nox supervenit navigantibus nobis in Hadria circa mediam noctem suspicabantur nautae apparere sibi aliquam regionem
clem: Sed posteaquam quartadecima nox supervenit, navigantibus nobis in Adria circa mediam noctem, suspicabantur naut apparere sibi aliquam regionem.
tr: ως δε τεσσαρεσκαιδεκατη νυξ εγενετο διαφερομενων ημων εν τω αδρια κατα μεσον της νυκτος υπενοουν οι ναυται προσαγειν τινα αυτοις χωραν
kjv: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;

vulg: qui submittentes invenerunt passus viginti et pusillum inde separati invenerunt passus quindecim
clem: Qui et summittentes bolidem, invenerunt passus viginti: et pusillum inde separati, invenerunt passus quindecim.
tr: και βολισαντες ευρον οργυιας εικοσι βραχυ δε διαστησαντες και παλιν βολισαντες ευρον οργυιας δεκαπεντε
kjv: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.

vulg: timentes autem ne in aspera loca incideremus de puppi mittentes anchoras quattuor optabant diem fieri
clem: Timentes autem ne in aspera loca incideremus, de puppi mittentes anchoras quatuor, optabant diem fieri.
tr: φοβουμενοι τε μηπως εις τραχεις τοπους εκπεσωσιν  εκπεσωμεν  εκ πρυμνης ριψαντες αγκυρας τεσσαρας ηυχοντο ημεραν γενεσθαι
kjv: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

vulg: nautis vero quaerentibus fugere de navi cum misissent scapham in mare sub obtentu quasi a prora inciperent anchoras extendere
clem: Nautis vero qurentibus fugere de navi, cum misissent scapham in mare, sub obtentu quasi inciperent a prora anchoras extendere,
tr: των δε ναυτων ζητουντων φυγειν εκ του πλοιου και χαλασαντων την σκαφην εις την θαλασσαν προφασει ως εκ πρωρας μελλοντων αγκυρας εκτεινειν
kjv: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,

vulg: dixit Paulus centurioni et militibus nisi hii in navi manserint vos salvi fieri non potestis
clem: dixit Paulus centurioni et militibus: Nisi hi in navi manserint, vos salvi fieri non potestis.
tr: ειπεν ο παυλος τω εκατονταρχη και τοις στρατιωταις εαν μη ουτοι μεινωσιν εν τω πλοιω υμεις σωθηναι ου δυνασθε
kjv: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.

vulg: tunc absciderunt milites funes scaphae et passi sunt eam excidere
clem: Tunc absciderunt milites funes scaph, et passi sunt eam excidere.
tr: τοτε οι στρατιωται απεκοψαν τα σχοινια της σκαφης και ειασαν αυτην εκπεσειν
kjv: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

vulg: et cum lux inciperet fieri rogabat Paulus omnes sumere cibum dicens quartadecima hodie die expectantes ieiuni permanetis nihil accipientes
clem: Et cum lux inciperet fieri, rogabat Paulus omnes sumere cibum, dicens: Quartadecima die hodie exspectantes jejuni permanetis, nihil accipientes.
tr: αχρι δε ου εμελλεν ημερα γινεσθαι παρεκαλει ο παυλος απαντας μεταλαβειν τροφης λεγων τεσσαρεσκαιδεκατην σημερον ημεραν προσδοκωντες ασιτοι διατελειτε μηδεν προσλαβομενοι
kjv: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.

vulg: propter quod rogo vos accipere cibum pro salute vestra quia nullius vestrum capillus de capite peribit
clem: Propter quod rogo vos accipere cibum pro salute vestra: quia nullius vestrum capillus de capite peribit.
tr: διο παρακαλω υμας προσλαβειν τροφης τουτο γαρ προς της υμετερας σωτηριας υπαρχει ουδενος γαρ υμων θριξ εκ της κεφαλης πεσειται
kjv: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.

vulg: et cum haec dixisset sumens panem gratias egit Deo in conspectu omnium et cum fregisset coepit manducare
clem: Et cum hc dixisset, sumens panem, gratias egit Deo in conspectu omnium: et cum fregisset, cpit manducare.
tr: ειπων δε ταυτα και λαβων αρτον ευχαριστησεν τω θεω ενωπιον παντων και κλασας ηρξατο εσθιειν
kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.

vulg: animaequiores autem facti omnes et ipsi adsumpserunt cibum
clem: Animquiores autem facti omnes, et ipsi sumpserunt cibum.
tr: ευθυμοι δε γενομενοι παντες και αυτοι προσελαβοντο τροφης
kjv: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.

vulg: eramus vero universae animae in navi ducentae septuaginta sex
clem: Eramus vero univers anim in navi ducent septuaginta sex.
tr: ημεν δε εν τω πλοιω αι πασαι ψυχαι διακοσιαι εβδομηκονταεξ
kjv: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.

vulg: et satiati cibo adleviabant navem iactantes triticum in mare
clem: Et satiati cibo alleviabant navem, jactantes triticum in mare.
tr: κορεσθεντες δε τροφης εκουφιζον το πλοιον εκβαλλομενοι τον σιτον εις την θαλασσαν
kjv: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.

vulg: cum autem dies factus esset terram non agnoscebant sinum vero quendam considerabant habentem litus in quem cogitabant si possent eicere navem
clem: Cum autem dies factus esset, terram non agnoscebant: sinum vero quemdam considerabant habentem littus, in quem cogitabant si possent ejicere navem.
tr: οτε δε ημερα εγενετο την γην ουκ επεγινωσκον κολπον δε τινα κατενοουν εχοντα αιγιαλον εις ον εβουλευσαντο ει δυναιντο εξωσαι το πλοιον
kjv: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.

vulg: et cum anchoras abstulissent committebant se mari simul laxantes iuncturas gubernaculorum et levato artemone secundum flatum aurae tendebant ad litus
clem: Et cum anchoras sustulissent, committebant se mari, simul laxantes juncturas gubernaculorum: et levato artemone secundum aur flatum, tendebant ad littus.
tr: και τας αγκυρας περιελοντες ειων εις την θαλασσαν αμα ανεντες τας ζευκτηριας των πηδαλιων και επαραντες τον αρτεμονα τη πνεουση κατειχον εις τον αιγιαλον
kjv: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.

vulg: et cum incidissemus in locum bithalassum inpegerunt navem et prora quidem fixa manebat inmobilis puppis vero solvebatur a vi maris
clem: Et cum incidissemus in locum dithalassum, impegerunt navem: et prora quidem fixa manebat immobilis, puppis vero solvebatur a vi maris.
tr: περιπεσοντες δε εις τοπον διθαλασσον επωκειλαν την ναυν και η μεν πρωρα ερεισασα εμεινεν ασαλευτος η δε πρυμνα ελυετο υπο της βιας των κυματων
kjv: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.

vulg: militum autem consilium fuit ut custodias occiderent ne quis cum enatasset effugeret
clem: Militum autem consilium fuit ut custodias occiderent, ne quis cum enatasset, effugeret.
tr: των δε στρατιωτων βουλη εγενετο ινα τους δεσμωτας αποκτεινωσιν μη τις εκκολυμβησας διαφυγοι
kjv: And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

vulg: centurio autem volens servare Paulum prohibuit fieri iussitque eos qui possent natare mittere se primos et evadere et ad terram exire
clem: Centurio autem volens servare Paulum, prohibuit fieri: jussitque eos qui possent natare, emittere se primos, et evadere, et ad terram exire:
tr: ο δε εκατονταρχος βουλομενος διασωσαι τον παυλον εκωλυσεν αυτους του βουληματος εκελευσεν τε τους δυναμενους κολυμβαν απορριψαντας πρωτους επι την γην εξιεναι
kjv: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:

vulg: et ceteros alios in tabulis ferebant quosdam super ea quae de navi essent et sic factum est ut omnes animae evaderent ad terram
clem: et ceteros, alios in tabulis ferebant, quosdam super ea qu de navi erant. Et sic factum est, ut omnes anim evaderent ad terram.
tr: και τους λοιπους ους μεν επι σανισιν ους δε επι τινων των απο του πλοιου και ουτως εγενετο παντας διασωθηναι επι την γην
kjv: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.

vulg: et cum evasissemus tunc cognovimus quia Militene insula vocatur barbari vero praestabant non modicam humanitatem nobis
clem: Et cum evasissemus, tunc cognovimus quia Melita insula vocabatur. Barbari vero prstabant non modicam humanitatem nobis.
tr: και διασωθεντες τοτε επεγνωσαν οτι μελιτη η νησος καλειται
kjv: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.

vulg: accensa enim pyra reficiebant nos omnes propter imbrem qui inminebat et frigus
clem: Accensa enim pyra, reficiebant nos omnes propter imbrem qui imminebat, et frigus.
tr: οι δε βαρβαροι παρειχον ου την τυχουσαν φιλανθρωπιαν ημιν αναψαντες γαρ πυραν προσελαβοντο παντας ημας δια τον υετον τον εφεστωτα και δια το ψυχος
kjv: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

vulg: cum congregasset autem Paulus sarmentorum aliquantam multitudinem et inposuisset super ignem vipera a calore cum processisset invasit manum eius
clem: Cum congregasset autem Paulus sarmentorum aliquantam multitudinem, et imposuisset super ignem, vipera a calore cum processisset, invasit manum ejus.
tr: συστρεψαντος δε του παυλου φρυγανων πληθος και επιθεντος επι την πυραν εχιδνα εκ της θερμης εξελθουσα καθηψεν της χειρος αυτου
kjv: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

vulg: ut vero viderunt barbari pendentem bestiam de manu eius ad invicem dicebant utique homicida est homo hic qui cum evaserit de mari Ultio non sinit vivere
clem: Ut vero viderunt barbari pendentem bestiam de manu ejus, ad invicem dicebant: Utique homicida est homo hic, qui cum evaserit de mari, ultio non sinit eum vivere.
tr: ως δε ειδον οι βαρβαροι κρεμαμενον το θηριον εκ της χειρος αυτου ελεγον προς αλληλους παντως φονευς εστιν ο ανθρωπος ουτος ον διασωθεντα εκ της θαλασσης η δικη ζην ουκ ειασεν
kjv: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.

vulg: et ille quidem excutiens bestiam in ignem nihil mali passus est
clem: Et ille quidem excutiens bestiam in ignem, nihil mali passus est.
tr: ο μεν ουν αποτιναξας το θηριον εις το πυρ επαθεν ουδεν κακον
kjv: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.

vulg: at illi existimabant eum in tumorem convertendum et subito casurum et mori diu autem illis sperantibus et videntibus nihil mali in eo fieri convertentes se dicebant eum esse deum
clem: At illi existimabant eum in tumorem convertendum, et subito casurum et mori. Diu autem illis exspectantibus, et videntibus nihil mali in eo fieri, convertentes se, dicebant eum esse deum.
tr: οι δε προσεδοκων αυτον μελλειν πιμπρασθαι η καταπιπτειν αφνω νεκρον επι πολυ δε αυτων προσδοκωντων και θεωρουντων μηδεν ατοπον εις αυτον γινομενον μεταβαλλομενοι ελεγον θεον αυτον ειναι
kjv: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

vulg: in locis autem illis erant praedia principis insulae nomine Publii qui nos suscipiens triduo benigne exhibuit
clem: In locis autem illis erant prdia principis insul, nomine Publii, qui nos suscipiens, triduo benigne exhibuit.
tr: εν δε τοις περι τον τοπον εκεινον υπηρχεν χωρια τω πρωτω της νησου ονοματι ποπλιω ος αναδεξαμενος ημας τρεις ημερας φιλοφρονως εξενισεν
kjv: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.

vulg: contigit autem patrem Publii febribus et dysenteria vexatum iacere ad quem Paulus intravit et cum orasset et inposuisset ei manus salvavit eum
clem: Contigit autem patrem Publii febribus et dysenteria vexatum jacere. Ad quem Paulus intravit: et cum orasset, et imposuisset ei manus, salvavit eum.
tr: εγενετο δε τον πατερα του ποπλιου πυρετοις και δυσεντερια συνεχομενον κατακεισθαι προς ον ο παυλος εισελθων και προσευξαμενος επιθεις τας χειρας αυτω ιασατο αυτον
kjv: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.

vulg: quo facto et omnes qui in insula habebant infirmitates accedebant et curabantur
clem: Quo facto, omnes qui in insula habebant infirmitates, accedebant, et curabantur:
tr: τουτου ουν γενομενου και οι λοιποι οι εχοντες ασθενειας εν τη νησω προσηρχοντο και εθεραπευοντο
kjv: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:

vulg: qui etiam multis honoribus nos honoraverunt et navigantibus inposuerunt quae necessaria erant
clem: qui etiam multis honoribus nos honoraverunt, et navigantibus imposuerunt qu necessaria erant.
tr: οι και πολλαις τιμαις ετιμησαν ημας και αναγομενοις επεθεντο τα προς την χρειαν
kjv: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.

vulg: post menses autem tres navigavimus in nave alexandrina quae in insula hiemaverat cui erat insigne Castorum
clem: Post menses autem tres navigavimus in navi Alexandrina, qu in insula hiemaverat, cui erat insigne Castorum.
tr: μετα δε τρεις μηνας ανηχθημεν εν πλοιω παρακεχειμακοτι εν τη νησω αλεξανδρινω παρασημω διοσκουροις
kjv: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.

vulg: et cum venissemus Syracusam mansimus ibi triduo
clem: Et cum venissemus Syracusam, mansimus ibi triduo.
tr: και καταχθεντες εις συρακουσας επεμειναμεν ημερας τρεις
kjv: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.

vulg: inde circumlegentes devenimus Regium et post unum diem flante austro secunda die venimus Puteolos
clem: Inde circumlegentes devenimus Rhegium: et post unum diem, flante austro, secunda die venimus Puteolos:
tr: οθεν περιελθοντες κατηντησαμεν εις ρηγιον και μετα μιαν ημεραν επιγενομενου νοτου δευτεραιοι ηλθομεν εις ποτιολους
kjv: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:

vulg: ubi inventis fratribus rogati sumus manere apud eos dies septem et sic venimus Romam
clem: ubi inventis fratribus rogati sumus manere apud eos dies septem: et sic venimus Romam.
